title: Nicotine Is Mounting a Comeback in the Wellness Movement
gist: A pulmonary physician-scientist (republished from The Conversation) argues that wellness influencers, podcasts and tech startups are rebranding nicotine, mainly via non-combustible formats like nicotine pouches and nicotine-caffeine-nootropic blends, as a focus, mood and longevity aid, and that the human evidence does not support those claims. The piece is a medical rebuttal: it names no companies or brands (no Zyn or Philip Morris) and gives no market-size or sales data, so its investable signal is limited to the cultural reframing trend and the scientific and regulatory counter-narrative forming against it.

insights.claim: Wellness personalities, podcasts, natural-medicine communities and tech startups are recasting nicotine as a misunderstood, performance-enhancing compound, a trend the author calls ironic because it is growing alongside the 'Make America Healthy Again' movement.
insights.speaker: Hasmeena Kathuria
insights.so_what: A cultural tailwind for non-combustible nicotine demand among health-conscious consumers who would never have smoked; watch whether it widens the user base beyond former smokers.
insights.quote: An ironic development emerging alongside the “Make America Healthy Again” movement is the portrayal of nicotine as a wellness and performance-enhancing product.

insights.claim: Nicotine's wellness comeback is carried by non-smoking formats such as nicotine pouches and by products that combine nicotine with caffeine and nootropics marketed as cognition enhancers.
insights.speaker: Hasmeena Kathuria
insights.so_what: The growth vector is pouch and functional-blend products, not cigarettes, so exposure means oral nicotine and 'smart' stimulant startups, not combustible volume.
insights.locator: Nicotine’s comeback as a wellness product

insights.claim: Part of the pro-nicotine reframing rests on nicotine being a 'natural' plant compound, found mainly in tobacco and in trace amounts in nightshade vegetables such as tomatoes, potatoes and eggplant.
insights.speaker: Hasmeena Kathuria
insights.so_what: The 'natural compound' framing is the marketing lever that lets nicotine enter wellness channels, and it is the likely target of any regulatory crackdown on health claims.
insights.locator: Some of this rebranding stems from

insights.claim: Proponents separate nicotine from cigarettes by pointing out that most smoking harm comes from burning tobacco, which produces thousands of toxic substances including carcinogens, carbon monoxide and fine particulate matter, rather than from nicotine itself.
insights.speaker: Hasmeena Kathuria
insights.so_what: The combustion-versus-nicotine split underpins the harm-reduction case for smoke-free products; the author accepts the premise but rejects the step from 'less harmful' to 'healthy'.
insights.locator: The greatest health risks arise when

insights.claim: Even without combustion, nicotine activates the sympathetic 'fight or flight' system, raising heart rate and blood pressure, disrupting sleep and adding strain on the heart with repeated use, with particular risk during developmental stages.
insights.speaker: Hasmeena Kathuria
insights.so_what: Cardiovascular, sleep and youth-exposure harms give regulators grounds to act against pouches and blends even if combustion harms are absent.
insights.locator: Nicotine activates the sympathetic nervous system

insights.claim: Nicotine creates dependence by acting on acetylcholine receptors; with repeated exposure the brain adds more nicotine receptors to make up for reduced responsiveness and releases dopamine, which reinforces reward.
insights.speaker: Hasmeena Kathuria
insights.so_what: Addiction is the core of the business model for recurring-revenue nicotine products, and also the main reason for regulatory and reputational risk.
insights.locator: With repeated exposure, the brain adapts

insights.claim: Evidence that nicotine enhances attention, vigilance, reaction time or memory is mixed; any benefit may be limited to people with mild cognitive impairment, and in healthy people nicotine appears to give no boost and may impair higher performers.
insights.speaker: Hasmeena Kathuria
insights.so_what: Focus and productivity marketing, the core pitch to tech and knowledge-worker buyers, has weak scientific support and is exposed to claims enforcement.
insights.quote: For healthy individuals, it doesn’t appear to offer any boost and may even worsen cognitive operation among higher-performing people.

insights.claim: Many nicotine-cognition studies enroll people who already depend on nicotine, so apparent gains may simply reverse withdrawal symptoms (irritability, anxiety, impaired attention) rather than show real enhancement.
insights.speaker: Hasmeena Kathuria
insights.so_what: Withdrawal relief looks like a benefit to users, which explains strong retention while undercutting efficacy claims.
insights.locator: In addition, many of these studies

insights.claim: Nicotine gives only temporary pleasure and stress relief; long-term users often find stress and anxiety harder to manage, and quitting is consistently linked to less anxiety, depression and stress and a better quality of life.
insights.speaker: Hasmeena Kathuria
insights.so_what: Mood-support positioning runs against the research consensus, a weak point if regulators or plaintiffs challenge wellness marketing.
insights.locator: Long-term users of nicotine often find

insights.claim: The most ambitious pro-nicotine claims, protection against Parkinson's, Alzheimer's and age-related cognitive decline, plus slower biological aging, rest only on lab studies of oxidative stress and animal studies of inflammation, which have not translated into human evidence.
insights.speaker: Hasmeena Kathuria
insights.so_what: Longevity-branded nicotine products are making claims with no human evidence behind them, which leaves them most exposed to regulatory or reputational backlash.
insights.quote: such findings have not translated into anything that indicates nicotine promotes healthy aging, extends lifespan or prevents age-related disease in humans.
insights.locator: There’s some kernels of research underneath

insights.claim: Medical researchers who study nicotine addiction are publicly pushing back on wellness-driven nicotine claims, which points to a growing scientific counter-narrative against the category.
insights.speaker: Hasmeena Kathuria
insights.so_what: Watch for physician and public-health pushback turning into policy, such as limits on health claims, flavor or marketing rules, and pouch regulation, which would be a headwind for the category.
insights.quote: As a pulmonary physician-scientist who studies nicotine addiction and the health consequences of tobacco and nicotine products, I am concerned about these claims.
